newsitem.title: UK: Former UK PM Thatcher denies she backing Portillo.
newsitem.headline: Former UK PM Thatcher denies she backing Portillo.

text.p: Former prime minister Margaret Thatcher's private office on Wednesday firmly denied a newspaper report that she was backing a secret Conservative party leadership campaign by Defence Secretary Michael Portillo.

The head of her private office said a report in the Daily Express saying she circulated a dossier on Conservative members of parliament and parliamentary candidates to help Portillo's campaign was "malicious nonsense and totally without foundation".
Julian Seymour added in the letter, issued to the media, that he wanted an apology and a full retraction by the Express.

Seymour added: "No such dossier, if it exists, was prepared either by her staff or with her authority. Lady Thatcher gives her full support to the prime minister and will work for victory by the Conservative Party at the forthcoming election."
Thatcher was ousted in 1990 after fears her leadership style and hostile attitude to Europe was costing the party votes. She was replaced as party leader and prime minister by John Major.
But polls tip the opposition Labour party to win the election Major must hold by May. A defeat for the Conservatives is likely to spark a bitter fight for the party leadership.

Portillo is widely seen as one of the leading candidates in a leadership battle, and media reports have consistently described him as having been groomed for leadership by Thatcher. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7768
